forecast-period.text: A high pressure ridge lies over central and eastern SA, while a low pressure trough moves over the far west late Thursday and Friday. A high pressure system will move over waters to the south over the weekend to be centred over southern Victoria by late Sunday, extending a ridge across SA until Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible patchy morning frost and fog on and east of the Flinders and Mount Lofty Ranges. Showers about the far west and the chance of an isolated shower about the far southeast. Possible thunderstorms about the far west during the afternoon and evening, possibly severe near the western border with the chance of damaging wind gusts, large hail and heavy rainfall. Maximum temperatures mostly above average, tending near average in the northeast. Generally light winds about the Agricultural Area, tending northeast to southeasterly in the north and west.
Dry apart from isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far west during the evening. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the northeast.

Morning fog patches about the southern coastal districts. Dry apart from the chance of a shower or thunderstorm near the far southwestern border. Maximum temperatures above average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the far northeast.
Morning fog patches about the agricultural area. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures above average. East to southeasterly winds, tending northeasterly about the west.

text.p: Morning fog patches on and east of the ranges and about Eastern Eyre Peninsula. Dry and mostly sunny day. Warmer, with above average maximum temperatures. East to southeasterly winds, tending north to northeasterly about the west, extending throughout during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: Less than 2 mm about the far southeast and windward coasts and ranges. 2 to 5 mm is likely in the far west, but local falls of 5 to 15 mm are possible. Isolated falls of 15 to 30 mm are possible near the western border with thunderstorms.
